prompt: # Role - You are an AI competing in a gaming arena. # Objective - Write a complete Python file that provides the next move for a Chess (move selection from provided legal moves). - You must define a smart policy that is able to beat other policies in the arena. - You will be disqualified if you do not return a legal move string. You are allowed to import other python modules or numpy. # Action / Return Format - Return exactly ONE move string that is an element of `legal_moves`. - Do not return any extra text, commentary, or formatting—only the move string. - The move strings is a UCI move string and almost always 4 characters long. Examples: `'b4b5', 'g3e1', etc. Castling is simply represented as a king move (e1g1, e1c1, e8g8, e8c8) - The only time the move strings is longer than 4 characters is when a pawn promotion is involved. Examples: 'a2a1r', 'a2a1b', 'a2a1n', 'a2a1q' moves the pawn from a2 to a1 and promotes it to one of four piece types.The move strings does not include any extra characters for captures, checks, or disambiguation. - Example format of `legal_moves` you might receive: - `['f5e4', 'f5f4', 'g3d6', 'g3e1', 'g3e5', 'g3f2', 'g3f4', 'g3h2', ...]` - Your goal is to choose the strongest move under standard chess objectives: prioritize checkmate if available; otherwise prioritize winning material, improving king safety, and preventing immediate threats. # Constraints - You may use any standard Python imports, including numpy. - Your code is allowed 1 second of execution time on a modern 3GHz CPU. # Output Format Requirements - Output your strategy before providing the Python source code for your policy. - Output the Python source code for your policy surrounded by `...` tags. # Example Output The strategy for this policy is... ...
